constraints_found: Of the ~57 labs the tab reads, only CRP (LBXCRP), HbA1c (LBXGH) and FastingGlucose (LBDSGLSI, only when the text says fasting) have a path to any patient-form conclusion. There are no other labs 'that already have cause edges' in the patient stack: no lab symbol other than these appears in any patient-stack .metta file (grep). So 'add KB markers for labs with cause edges' is already done; anything more needs new curated edges.

Biomarker symbols with a Pos path from a cause (usable by diagnose-patient): CRP, DNAmGDF15, DNAmPAI1, FastingGlucose, HbA1c, DNAmPACKYRS. Non-biomarker nodes that also work as observations: CoronaryHeartDisease, InsulinResistance, ChronicInflammation, SASP. Symbols with a Neg path from the default supplement pool (Omega3 Berberine Fisetin NMN Resveratrol): CRP, DNAmGDF15, DNAmPAI1, FastingGlucose, HbA1c, CoronaryHeartDisease, InsulinResistance (not DNAmPACKYRS). diagnose-patient, recommend-supplements-patient and rank-interventions-for-patient read only patient-observations (patient_profile.metta:277-287 for markers with z > 1.0, built from MeasuredZ/MeasuredRaw). explains-obs credits only Pos chains (pln_abductive_diagnosis.metta:43-45). Runtime, not head symbols, is the binding constraint for adding markers. recommend-supplements-patient on the tab default patient took 5.4 s, then 17.5 / 40.0 / 65.9 s with +4 / +8 / +12 extra MeasuredZ (57.7 s at +12 even with z=0.2). +57 ran for more than 10 min and was killed (no abort observed). Head-symbol margin: one new patient head (HasDiagnosis or PatientCondition) plus 32 padding heads ran rc=0 for diagnose, supplements and rank in the patient stack, and new symbols in argument position (WhiteBloodCellCount etc.) did not abort. No probe in this scout aborted.

MeasuredZ argument types are not enforced. A MeasuredZ on an Outcome or Phenotype (CoronaryHeartDisease, InsulinResistance) is accepted and grounded like a lab, which is why a dedicated condition head is preferable to faking a z.

verdict.corrections:
The claim holds: the effect reproduces exactly, the evidence lines are right, it adds 0 head symbols, and the biology is stated in the KB. Five things in it need correcting or adding.

1. "Currently comes back empty" is a conditional, and I could not test the live translator. There is no OPENAI_API_KEY (pln_chat/core/llm_translator.py:18,123), so the translator cannot run here. The battery entry that already uses the broad list (scripts/linage2_battery.py:542-545, docs/linage2_battery/results.json:516-524) stubs the translator (linage2_battery.py:611-615). Its "pass" therefore does not show that the translator emits that list.

2. A new piece the claim misses: the question can be sent to the wrong form. The tab patient always has LinAge2. Rule 16 (pln_chat/prompts/system_prompt.txt:193-194) maps "what are the main drivers of my biological age" to (linage-drivers-patient ...). The per-patient hint (pln_chat/core/patient_context.py:113-130) lists linage-drivers-patient and does not mention diagnose-patient. "What is the likely DRIVER of my abnormal labs?" (patient_tab.py:52) is close in wording, so the translator may send it to linage-drivers-patient. The new prompt rule must separate "drivers of my biological age" (LinAge2) from "cause of my abnormal labs" (diagnose-patient). The rule fits as rule 17 after rule 16 (which ends about :214), or next to rule 13 (:105-121). Ideally the hint at patient_context.py:113-130 also gets a diagnose line. The code comment at patient_tab.py:44-45 says every suggested question maps to rule 16 or the hint. That is false today for this question.

3. "Their elevated labs ... are never looked at" is overstated. The supplement layer and LinAge2's DrivenBy also use the CRP/HbA1c witnesses (battery E1 #44, results.json:507-509). Only the diagnosis path misses them, and only when the few-shot list is copied. When the few-shot list does run on the tab patient, the answer is a bare `()` with no warning saying that no listed cause explains HbA1c or glucose (E2E probe 1). Adding that warning is an optional extra.

4. SmokingPackYears is only inert for tab patients. The tab never emits DNAmPACKYRS: patient_text.kb_markers emits only CRP, HbA1c and FastingGlucose (core/patient_text.py:279-296). But API callers can send DNAmPACKYRS (core/patient_builder.py:123). For Patient003 the broad list returns (Hypothesis SmokingPackYears (stv 0.8 0.6) 1 0.48 (SupportedBy (DNAmPACKYRS))) as its only hypothesis. So it belongs in a general default.

5. The test note is wrong. No test reads few_shot_examples.json; the only reader is pln_chat/core/context_builder.py:24-25. The tests that use this list hard-code it themselves: test_pln_deduction.py:252-267 (population `diagnose`), test_patient_stack.py:39,113, test_patient_grounding.py:130. Changing the few-shot needs no test change.

Evidence checked:
- few_shot_examples.json:185: correct.
- system_prompt.txt: grep -i diagnos finds nothing; the risk rule is at :92-98 and the supplement rule at :105-112.
- pln_abductive_diagnosis.metta:147-149: correct.
- pln_supplement_recommendation.metta:225-227: correct.
- mechanistic_bridges.metta:180-185: correct. The comment at :176-178 says outright that this edge gives diagnosis a metabolic cause, at AnimalStudies_Replicated confidence. These are the only incoming harmful edges to InsulinResistance, FastingGlucose and HbA1c (Metformin and Berberine at :199 and :201 are protective, Neg).
- diagnose-patient itself is at patient_profile.metta:301-302. The default form goes after :302.

Head symbols: 0 is right. The repo defines a head symbol as the first element of an atom, and a rule's head is `=` (docs/nhanes_integration.md:408-412). I also measured it. With the rule in the full shared stack plus 4 budget-probe definitions (the ceiling test, tests/test_smoking_lever.py:398-419), predict-risk-patient Patient001 still answers. In the patient stack, the rule plus 32 ProbeHead pads also answers. (Side note: that test's docstring, :380-381, says +5 definitions abort. Today +5 runs, rc=0, so the docstring is stale.)

Naming: `diagnose-patient-default` does not match `_PATIENT_FACT_RE`, whose `-patient` must be the end of the name (patient_context.py:72-74). It still routes to the patient stack because the program names Caller_Me (names_a_patient, :60-66). A better option is a 2-argument overload `(= (diagnose-patient $space $patient) (diagnose-patient $space $patient (...)))`. It adds no new symbol at all, has the same shape as recommend-supplements-patient, and leaves the 3-argument form unchanged (probe: the few-shot list still returns `()`).

Smaller risk: diagnose ignores how large z is. For the 'six labs only' example (CRP z 1.18, HbA1c z 3.2), ChronicInflammation (mass 0.52) ranks above InsulinResistance (0.455).

Effort S stands: a prompt rule, a hint line, a few-shot update, and an optional one-rule default form. It needs no test changes; adding one test for the new default form would be good.

verdict.corrections:
The claim holds: every number it states reproduces, the cited lines exist and say what is claimed, and the count of 1 new head (PatientCondition) is honest. But it is not a quick win. Corrections:

1. Off-by-one citation. The compute_linage2 call is at pln_chat/core/patient_text.py:324-325, not 323-324. The questionnaire is also copied for display at :338-339 and its notes are shown in pln_chat/patient_tab.py:106, but it is not reasoned over anywhere else. _DIAGNOSES is :469-495 (:468 is the comment). All other evidence lines check out: patient_profile.metta:277-287 and :301-302, :335-339, :347-348; pln_supplement_recommendation.metta:101-106; grim_age_lu2019_evidence.metta:10-12, :44-51, :58-59; mechanistic_bridges.metta:171, :180, :191, :199-202; pln_deduction.metta:113-117; patient_builder.py:666-678.

2. Biology: the CHD half is stated in the KB. The diabetes half is not.
   - CHD is a KB Outcome (grim_age_lu2019_evidence.metta:11).
   - Its explainers are KB paths:
     - InsulinResistance->FastingGlucose->CHD (mechanistic_bridges.metta:182, :191; the last link is a curated Epidemiological prior, which :189-190 itself calls the thing to upgrade).
     - CellularSenescence->SASP->DNAmPAI1->CHD (mechanistic_bridges.metta:53, :56 plus the Lu2019 HR 1.31 record). That last link is a predictive DNAm association that infer uses as a causal step.
   - "Diabetes = InsulinResistance" exists nowhere in the KB. No Diabetes or Type2Diabetes symbol occurs in any non-LinAge2 .metta file; it appears only in comorbidity text at linage2_core.metta:232 and in López-Otín evidence text. The mapping would live only in Python, so it must be documented as an app-side translation.
   - T1D risk confirmed by running the reader: "type 1 diabetes" gives DIQ010=1, and the note says just "diagnoses: diabetes" (patient_text.py:471), so the type is lost.

3. Double counting is worse than the claim says.
   - Rank form: every candidate's score exactly doubles, not just D+Q. Base patient: Metformin 0.0886->0.1772, Berberine 0.0768->0.1536, D+Q 0.0425->0.0851. The order is unchanged, so on a patient with no labs a CHD observation adds no information to the CHD ranking.
   - Unflagged by the scout: on the tab default patient, the InsulinResistance observation double counts the HbA1c and FastingGlucose labs that already show it.
     - Supplements: Berberine goes 0.388 -> 0.830 from IR alone (+0.442), more than both labs together (0.388).
     - Rank: Metformin goes 0.648 -> 1.374 (+0.6375 from the direct Metformin->IR link, +0.0886 from CHD).
     - Diagnose: the top hypothesis flips from InsulinResistance (coverage 2) to DeregulatedNutrientSensing (coverage 3).
     - Cause: an observation one hop upstream escapes the per-hop confidence attenuation, so one typed word outweighs two measured labs.
   - Excluding the outcome in the rank form does not fix this. Fix it in patient-relevance / supp-targets (patient_profile.metta:335-339, pln_supplement_recommendation.metta:101-106), for example by dropping a condition already witnessed by an elevated downstream marker. Or ship CHD first and defer the diabetes->IR mapping.

4. Missing pieces the scout did not list:
   a. pln_chat/core/patient_context.py:72-74 _PATIENT_FACT_RE must include PatientCondition. Otherwise a program like (match &self (PatientCondition $p ...)) is routed to the full stack, gets no session-patient atoms, and returns nothing.
   b. A (: PatientCondition ...) declaration is needed in patient_profile.metta (next to :91-93) so that api.py:589-604 _unknown_patient_warning does not report "PatientCondition" as an unknown patient id (its regex is (?:Patient|Caller_)\w*).
   c. API payload schema: pln_chat/api.py:1066 PatientIn and :1390 PatientOut, plus API.md.
   d. ParsedPatient.to_patient (patient_text.py:314-331) must put conditions in the payload.
   e. predict-risk-patient (pln_risk_prediction.metta:399-400) still predicts incident CHD for someone with a known CHD diagnosis. The answer or the tab needs to say so.

5. Head budget and placement:
   - The rule plus type line placed inside a scratch copy of patient_profile.metta keeps every full-stack control in tests/test_patient_stack.py as it is:
     - The 7 must-answer forms (P001 dx/risk/cf, P002 dx/risk, P003 rank/supp) still answer.
     - The 3 must-abort forms (P001 rank/supp, P002 supp) still abort.
     - P001's built-in rank is byte-identical (0.2306046747621094).
   - In the patient stack, the default patient plus both conditions plus 32 pads answers dx, supp and rank (rc=0), and 63 pads plus PatientCondition (64 new heads) still answers supp and rank.
   - Fragility: the same two lines appended after all KB files made all six full-stack patient forms abort (rc=-6), and appending only the extra atoms changes nothing else. So the change must land inside patient_profile.metta, and the full-stack controls must be re-run.

6. Effort: M at least. It touches 2 .metta files (patient_profile plus a double-count fix), patient_builder, patient_text (keeping the diabetes type), patient_context, the api schema, the prompt wording, and tests. Safer scope: CoronaryHeartDisease only (MCQ160C/D/E); defer the diabetes mapping until (3) is solved.

verdict.corrections:
The mechanism holds and the scout's probes reproduce exactly. Five things need correcting.

1) The default-example effect is overstated. The scout recommends the LinAge2 per-sex median/MAD. Against it, the tab default (58 M) gives:
- WBC 8.2: z = (ln 8.2 - 1.887)/0.2975 = 0.73, Normal.
- RDW 14.1: z = (14.1 - 12.5)/0.593 = 2.70, Elevated.
- TG 190 mg/dL (2.145 mmol/L): z is about 0.7-1.0 against the pooled NHANES quantiles [0.395, 1.344, 7.765] (data/linage2/linage2_model.json nhanes_central; 0.5/50/99.5 %, scripts/extract_linage2_model.py:246-248). That is not above the 1.0 cutoff (patient_profile.metta:151, 157-161).

So for the default example only RDW becomes a finding:
- Diagnosis adds ChronicInflammation (stv 0.5 0.6) and CellularSenescence.
- Omega3 becomes Tier1 with Targets (RedCellDistributionWidth), score 0.1377.
- Berberine is unchanged (Targets (HbA1c FastingGlucose)).
- Ranking: D+Q score goes 0.0425 to 0.0729; order unchanged.

The 'WBC 1.5, RDW 1.3, TG 1.6' z values in the scout's probe are not what the default text yields.

2) Triglycerides naming and reference. TG is not a LinAge2 feature; it is only an input to LDLV (pln_chat/core/linage2_model.py:265-270; json derived.LDLV). So no LinAge2 median/MAD exists for TG. The repo already reserves the symbol name 'Triglycerides' (not 'SerumTriglycerides'):
- nhanes_reference_etl.py:403-413 (LBXTR, Log10, emit=False)
- data/nhanes/MANIFEST.tsv:12-13
- data/nhanes/README.md:122-125
- docs/pipeline.md:470

Use that name. Add a non-fasting caveat like SerumGlucose (linage2_core.metta:254-260): the tab reads LBDSTRSI, the biochemistry-profile value (patient_text.py:86).

3) The builder docstring is not outdated. patient_builder.py:62-69 says no age/sex-stratified table exists. LinAge2's table is per-sex only, from a <=50-year-old 1999-2000 reference (scripts/extract_linage2_model.py:136; docs/linage2_integration.md:258, 296), so the docstring is still true.
- Reference (patient_builder.py:58-90) has no sex, and to_z(value) takes no sex, so a per-sex Reference needs a code change.
- The cheaper path: kb_markers (patient_text.py:288-311) computes z per sex and sends {"z": ...}. The builder accepts that for any MARKERS entry (patient_builder.py:342-399).
- LinAge2 already computes this z (linage2_model.py:297-300) but does not return it; contributions carry only years (:303-307).

4) Head-symbol risk. new_head_symbols = 0 is right, and the patient stack keeps its pad32 margin. But a new symbol inside an Effect atom is not free in the FULL shared stack, which loads mechanistic_bridges.metta (api.py:198, app.py:132):
- Injected after load as extra_atoms, the single edge (Effect ChronicInflammation WhiteBloodCellCount ...) aborts the full stack (rc -6, panic at hyperon-space/src/index/trie.rs:179 TrieKeyStorage::get_atom_unchecked). It aborts even non-patient queries: rank-interventions, infer Omega3 CRP.
- (Inheritance WhiteBloodCellCount Biomarker) and an Effect edge between existing symbols do not abort.
- Written into a copy of mechanistic_bridges.metta (file-level), the full stack answered with unchanged results.

So the edges must go in the file and never be injected into the full space. Re-run the full-stack canaries and tests/test_patient_stack.py. The NHANES stack (pln_runner.py:91) and the LinAge2 stack (:196) also load mechanistic_bridges.metta. The LinAge2 stack was checked: unchanged, and it survives pad16.

5) The biology is not in the KB. No atom or doc states WBC/RDW -> ChronicInflammation or TG -> InsulinResistance; docs/pipeline.md:470 has only a PhenoAge-TG correlation. The edges are new curated priors and need anchors under the honesty contract (mechanistic_bridges.metta:11-21; tier convention :23-27). Caveats:

- Smoking raises WBC, and the default patient is a smoker.

constraints_found: Only labs with a Pos Effect chain into them can change a shared patient answer. A lab MeasuredZ with no edge enters patient-observations and nothing else. Probed at z +2.5 for SerumAlbumin, RedCellDistributionWidth, NTproBNP, WhiteBloodCellCount, SerumCreatinine, UricAcid, BodyMassIndex, SystolicBloodPressure, CalculatedLDL, ALT, SerumGlucose, CurrentTobaccoExposure and LymphocytePercent: each changed obs only. diagnose-patient, recommend-supplements-patient, rank-interventions-for-patient, predict-risk-patient, decompose-grimage and counterfactual-patient were unchanged (all rc=0). Mechanism: pln_abductive_diagnosis.metta:43-45 (Pos-only explains), patient_profile.metta:318-321 (relevance clamp0).

Low z never matters. SerumAlbumin, LymphocytePercent and Hemoglobin at -2.5, and CRP -2.0, are all UNCHANGED, even with an (Effect ChronicInflammation SerumAlbumin Neg ...) edge. Only z > (elevated-z-threshold)=1.0 enters observations (patient_profile.metta:151, 277-283). Low-is-bad labs (albumin, HDL, haemoglobin, lymphocyte %) need a sign-flipped Elevated symbol plus a Pos edge, which was probed and works (alb_flip_edge).

The size of z above the threshold is irrelevant to diagnose, supplements and ranking. CRP z 2.0 and z 1.066 gave byte-identical answers, as did HbA1c 2.0 and 1.349. Witness quality is purely where the Elevated cut falls.

Witness placement is a policy question. With the current coarse priors (patient_builder.py:137-166), a 58-year-old man typing HbA1c 5.9 %, CRP 5 mg/L and fasting glucose 105 mg/dL gets z 0.8/0.92/0.83, and diagnose, supplements and the personal ranking term all return empty or population-only. LinAge2's median/MAD (data/linage2/linage2_model.json) is a <=50-year-old same-sex 1999-2000 reference (scripts/extract_linage2_model.py:16-20, 135-150). mu_z (the 40-85 training-cohort mean z) is about 0.97 for HbA1c and 0.86 for glucose in men, so 'young-ref' z overcalls older people. Per-age same-sex medians exist (pln_chat/core/linage2_model.py:99-106). For women, every LinAge2-derived CRP z calls 10 mg/L Normal, where the coarse prior calls it Elevated. No NHANES ReferenceDistribution numbers are in the repo (no build/; nhanes_reference.metta header).

predict-risk-patient reads only AgeAccelGrim (pln_risk_prediction.metta:193-194). decompose-grimage and counterfactual-patient read only (PartOf X GrimAge) components (pln_counterfactual.metta:150-153, 295; grim_age_core.metta:85-92). No lab can change these three.

Latency grows roughly with the cube of the marker count, whether the markers are Elevated or Normal. patient-observations alone took 1.2 s at 3 markers, 4.1 s at 10, 21.7 s at 20 (21.3 s with all Normal), 68.7 s at 30 and 547 s at 57. Never send inert labs. MAX_MARKERS=40 (patient_builder.py:188) is far past responsive.

Appending ANY single extra atom through extra_atoms (one Effect edge, one Inheritance fact, or one padding atom) aborts generic diagnose, rank-interventions and decompose-grimage with 'panicked at hyperon-space/src/index/trie.rs:179:71' (rc -6). The candidate edges do not change built-in patients. With all 5 edges added, Patient001 and Patient002 diagnose, supplements, ranking, counterfactual and risk were byte-identical, at the same runtime (about 27 s and 23 s).

The builder refuses any marker not in MARKERS. build_patient(markers={'SerumAlbumin': {'z': -2.0}}) raises unknown_marker (patient_builder.py:332-340). kb_markers sends only CRP, HbA1c and fasting-gated FastingGlucose (patient_text.py:288-296). The age- and sex-specific median (linage2_model.py:99-106, which gives 5.5 for a 58-year-old man) with the young-reference MAD of 0.4448 gives z 0.899 for 5.9 %. Probe s_h0899 shows that is byte-identical to the baseline, so nothing changes. Under Option A the Elevated cut for men becomes >5.745 % at 40-45, >5.945 % at 58-60 and >6.045 % at 65-70, which is stricter than today's >6.0 %. The z of 1.349 that produced the probed effect comes from the young-reference median and MAD (the <=50-year-old 1999-2000 same-sex reference, scripts/extract_linage2_model.py:135-150) without subtracting mu_z. Its cut is age-independent: 5.745 % for men and 5.645 % for women. That option is the one that matches the ADA 5.7 % cut, but the claim lists it only under risks, not as an option. It would also break the "age/sex-adjusted" meaning of MeasuredZ (patient_profile.metta:63-68): it adjusts for sex but not age.

1. The -6.14 y headline is not what this candidate delivers. RDW alone moves the ChronicInflammation lever from 0.0 to -2.7293555 y (signed Neg (stv 2.73 0.6), Via (RedCellDistributionWidth)). That is the edge strength 0.5 times RDW's 5.458711 y (pln_linage2.metta:296-319, `$red (* $s $y)`). The -6.136 y in labs_scout/out_l2.json also needs albumin's 6.81 y, through a separate readout (MeasuresBiomarker SerumAlbumin Hypoalbuminemia) and a second edge. SerumAlbumin has no edge anywhere in the KB today; grep finds only linage2_core.metta:209. Also unreported: the CellularSenescence lever goes 0.0 -> -1.972 y (conf 0.205). The Omega3 lever returns nothing in the LinAge2 stack, because supplement_evidence.metta is not in LINAGE2_PATIENT_STACK (pln_runner.py:187-206). The tab can recommend Omega3 but cannot put years on it.

2. "Largest CBC weight" is true for men only. Men: LBXRDW +14.77 months/SD, the largest CBC weight. Women: MCHC -16.22, MPV -14.90 and basophil% -14.37 all exceed RDW's +13.02 in magnitude (data/linage2/linage2_model.json, sex.*.w_months_per_sd). The rest of the cited model data checks out: median 12.5 / MAD 0.593 (men), 12.45 / 0.815 (women), z 5.0587 and 5.4587 y for 15.5 % in a man.

3. Evidence line corrections:
   - LINAGE2_PATIENT_STACK is pln_runner.py:187-206, with mechanistic_bridges at :196.
   - kb_markers is patient_text.py:279-312.
   - linage2_core.metta section 5 is :239-268.
   - Everything else cited exists and says what is claimed: linage2_core.metta:200; patient_text.py:112; pln_linage2.metta:87-88, :99-109, :132-143; epistemic_calibration.metta:36 = 0.60.

4. Missing pieces, corrected:
   (a) The drift test needs no change. drift() (patient_vocabulary.py:71-107) never reads MARKERS or MeasuresBiomarker.
   (b) A test that WILL break: tests/test_linage2.py:715 pins reads_out to {CRP, HbA1c, SerumGlucose, SerumCotinine}. linage2_builder.py:61 regex-parses linage2_core.metta, so /linage2/features picks up RDW automatically.
   (c) Stale counts to edit: linage2_core.metta:245 ("Only FOUR of the 59"), pln_linage2.metta:86 ("55 of 59") and docs/linage2_integration.md:264.
   (d) The Reference dataclass (patient_builder.py:59-90) holds one mean/sd and to_z gets no sex. Using LinAge2's sex-specific median/MAD needs a sex-aware Reference and _resolve_marker change, or a pooled value. Route RDW through the kb_markers loop (patient_text.py:298-311) so the Z_LIMIT cap applies. Without it, RDW >= 19.6 % in a man (z > 12) fails the whole build with implausible_z (patient_builder.py:393-399).
   (e) The edge needs (Inheritance RedCellDistributionWidth ...) only for readability. It is not required: the probes ran without one.

   Effort M is right.

5. The threshold risk is bigger than stated. Under the median/MAD reference, z > 1.0 (patient_profile.metta:151) calls RDW Elevated at about 13.09 % in men and 13.27 % in women. Subtracting mu_z (0.62 men, 0.40 women) moves this only to 13.46 / 13.59 %. Both are inside the usual ~11.5-14.5 % reference interval (general clinical knowledge, not stated in the KB). So many people with an ordinary RDW would get ChronicInflammation and an Omega3 Tier1 recommendation. The shared forms ignore magnitude once z > 1, so 13.2 % and 25 % give identical answers. docs/linage2_integration.md:257-260 already warns that the two z conventions only meet qualitatively. A clinical floor (for example RDW > 14.5 %) is safer.

   The anaemia gate the scout suggested is cheap: patient_text.py:79-83 already reads ferritin, folate and B12. It belongs in kb_markers, in Python.

6. Biology: the KB states no RDW biology today. The edge is new curation. According to PubMed, the anchor is accurate (Lippi et al. 2009, PMID 19391664, https://doi.org/10.5858/133.4.628): a retrospective study of 3845 outpatients, where hsCRP and ESR predicted RDW independently of age, sex, MCV, Hb and ferritin. It is an association, so the Epidemiological tier (0.60) fits. The paper does not give the causal direction, and the strength 0.5 is not derived from it; it is a judgment. That is allowed by the contract at mechanistic_bridges.metta:11-22, but the LinAge2 counterfactual turns this one number directly into years (0.5 x 5.46 y).

- `Epidemiological` exists (epistemic_calibration.metta:16,36; 0.60) and is already used at mechanistic_bridges.metta:192.
- PubMed 9600484 is correct (Danesh 1998, JAMA 279:1477-82). Leukocyte count RR 1.4 (1.3-1.5) for 8.4 vs 5.6 x10^9/L. The paper says the mechanisms "are not clear". It supports a WBC->CHD association. It does not support the edge ChronicInflammation->WBC or its strength. The 0.60 is a curated prior and must be labelled as one under the honesty contract (mechanistic_bridges.metta:119-121). The KB states no WBC biology today; this is new curation.

2. SIDE EFFECTS THE SCOUT DID NOT REPORT (all measured). The edge is reached through SASP->ChronicInflammation (mechanistic_bridges.metta:128-129).
- CellularSenescence also gains WBC (cov 1->2, conf 0.222->0.382). It moves ABOVE InsulinResistance in the differential.

verdict.corrections:
The mechanism works and every evidence line exists. Three things are overstated: what changes for the person, the reference, and the risk to the full stack.

1. **The effect is all-or-nothing at z > 1.0.** The threshold is set at patient_profile.metta:151 and applied in `elevated-marker` at patient_profile.metta:278-284.
   - z 0.9 changes nothing. z 1.1, 2.5 and 6.0 all give the same answer (diagnosis InsulinResistance (stv 0.6 0.6) 1.0 0.36, Berberine 0.143208, Metformin 0.29516).
   - So the only thing that matters is which triglyceride level crosses z = 1, and the claim never pins that down.

2. **McLaughlin's 1.47 mmol/L would not become a witness under any reference the repo can supply.**
   - "No MAD in the repo" is true: the LinAge2 median/mad lists are per feature, and LBDSTRSI is not a feature (extract_linage2_model.py:64).
   - But `nhanes_central` holds the 0.5th/50th/99.5th percentiles, both sexes (extract_linage2_model.py:243-248): [0.395, 1.344, 7.765] mmol/L. From these a pooled log-scale prior can be built today without the ETL: mean 1.344, ln-sd about 0.578 (about 0.681 if fitted to the upper tail only).
   - Under that prior, Elevated starts at about 2.40 mmol/L (212 mg/dL), or about 2.66 mmol/L with the upper-tail fit. 130 mg/dL gives z = 0.15 and 150 mg/dL gives z = 0.40, so neither is a witness.
   - The probe's z = 2.5 corresponds to about 5.6 mmol/L (500 mg/dL).
   - The tab's own "58-year-old smoker" example (patient_text.py:1113, TG 190 mg/dL) gets z ≈ 0.81, so it gains nothing.
   - Making 1.47 or 1.7 the threshold means picking mean/sd so that ln(cut/mean)/sd = 1. That is a cut-point dressed up as a distribution, because `Reference` (patient_builder.py:58-90) has no cut-point mode. This is a design decision that needs to be stated.
   - It would be the fourth coarse prior, not the third: CRP, FastingGlucose and HbA1c already have one (patient_builder.py:136-164).

3. **The biology is not in the KB; it is a new curated edge.**
   - No .metta file mentions Triglycerides.
   - The only KB-adjacent mentions are prose: docs/pipeline.md:470 (`CorrelatedWith (Elevated PhenoAge) (Elevated Triglycerides)`) and the LDL comment at linage2_core.metta:235.
   - According to PubMed the anchor is real: McLaughlin et al. 2003, PMID 14623617 ([DOI](https://doi.org/10.7326/0003-4819-139-10-200311180-00007)). It is a cross-sectional study of 258 non-diabetic, overweight adults with fasting lipids. The TG cut-point of 1.47 mmol/L had sensitivity 67% and specificity 71%.
   - stv 0.6 is the author's own prior, not a number taken from the paper. The direction (IR -> TG, Pos) matches the existing IR -> FastingGlucose and IR -> HbA1c pattern (mechanistic_bridges.metta:182-185).

4. **No new head symbols is confirmed, but the full stack is fragile.**
   - The edge as extra atoms in the full stack aborts: rc -6, panic at trie.rs:179:71, even on `!(infer &self Metformin CoronaryHeartDisease)`.
   - The no-extras control does not abort. A same-shaped `(Effect InsulinResistance CRP …)` does not, and `(Inheritance Triglycerides Biomarker)` alone does not.
   - Placed in mechanistic_bridges.metta after line 185 (tested in a scratchpad copy), the full stack answers 5 general (non-patient) queries.
   - In the same copy, these all pass: tests/test_patient_stack.py (37 passed, including the 32-head margin and the full-stack abort controls), the LinAge2 margin tests in tests/test_linage2.py (3 passed), and test_patient_vocabulary, test_caller_patients and test_patient_grounding (52 passed).
   - Add a full-stack general-query regression test, and never inject this edge as extra atoms.

5. **Smaller corrections.**
   - The ETL entry is nhanes_reference_etl.py:405-414 (`emit=False` is at :413).
   - TG is not a LinAge2 feature, but it still reaches LinAge2 through CalculatedLDL when LDL is not typed (linage2_model.py:265-273). The TG input is used by both parts, so the new edge is the only part that is shared-layer only.
   - The fasting flag is set only for glucose aliases (patient_text.py:154, 667), as the claim says.

**What is actually missing:**
- **KB:** add `(Inheritance Triglycerides Biomarker)` and the Effect edge with a citation comment in mechanistic_bridges.metta. 2 atoms, 0 new heads.
- **Builder:** add a `MARKERS["Triglycerides"]` entry with a `Reference` (patient_builder.py:97-165). This also lists it in GET /patients/markers.

- **Tests:** new tests for all of the above. tests/test_patient_text.py:223 does not include TG, so it stays green.

Effort M is fair. Most of it is the reference decision, not the code.

2. NO THIRD ATOM SET IS NEEDED. pln_runner.py:149-151 is accurate but irrelevant, because atoms go in per call as extra_atoms. The real missing pieces:
   - (a) A KB edit in patient_profile.metta:286-287 (patient-observations), plus (: PatientCondition (-> PatientProfile Outcome Atom)) after :93.
   - (b) A conditions key in the payload built by ParsedPatient.to_patient (patient_text.py:326-330). Today the payload has no condition field: the questionnaire goes only to compute_linage2 (patient_text.py:324-325).

   - (e) Tests.
   - Effort is S to M, not M because of a routing split, since that split already exists.

3. LEAK RISK IS OVERSTATED. "One leak aborts every generic question" is true in the full stack: (PatientCondition ...) aborts with rc -6 on infer, on rank-interventions and even on a plain (match &self (Inheritance CoronaryHeartDisease $x) $x), with or without the caller atoms. But no code path at HEAD puts shared_atoms there.

The engine half of the claim holds: comments add 0 head symbols and every answer stays identical. The proposal as written breaks validation for every patient question, and its evidence and labels need fixing.

1. **Wrong evidence line.** pln_chat/core/patient_context.py:120-123 sits inside linage2_prompt_hint. The atoms reach the translator at patient_context.py:144, in patient_prompt_section (134-149), which app.py:311 and api.py:3314 call.

2. **The precedent does not apply; comments in injected atoms fail validation.**
   - docs/linage2_integration.md:187-189 ("Codes as comments") is about comments in a KB file (linage2_core.metta). KB files go through the loader and are never passed to validate().
   - Injected patient atoms are. validation_text (patient_context.py:108-110) joins the atoms and the query.
   - validate() (pln_chat/core/metta_validator.py:161-182) blanks only strings and numbers, then tokenizes with _SYMBOL_RE (line 57), which also matches lowercase words. It never strips comments.
   - Result: every word in a ';;' line becomes an unknown symbol on every patient query. The chat prints "Validation Issues" (utils/formatting.py:40-42) every turn, through app.py:369-371, 390 and 414. /metta/run refuses with 422 (api.py:3562-3570; LinAge2 path api.py:3148).
   - The scout's "validator would flag them" therefore fires on the comments themselves, not only on LLM-invented symbols.

3. **The payload does not carry the diagnoses.**
   - to_patient (pln_chat/core/patient_text.py:326-330) sends only id, age, sex, smoking, markers and linage2.
   - The LinAge2 response (pln_chat/core/linage2_model.py:336-348) carries only the fs1Score years.
   - The chat rebuilds the patient from the stored payload every turn (app.py:296-301; patient_tab.py:242-261). So tab code rendering parsed.questionnaire would reach the build-time panel only, never the translator on later turns.
   - Real missing pieces:
     - a payload key such as diagnoses (a list of NHANES item codes), set in to_patient;
     - validation of that key against a closed list in build_patient (its docstring at patient_builder.py:448-449 says nothing is interpolated unchecked);
     - a BuiltPatient field (patient_builder.py:226-247);
     - the same field on PatientIn (api.py:1066-1084, extra="forbid") if /query and /patients/preview are to agree (patient_context.py:51-54).

4. **Two routes that work.**
   - (a) Keep atoms and shared_atoms free of comments. Add the diagnoses as prose in patient_prompt_section after the atoms (patient_context.py:140-149) and in the download header (patient_tab.py:190-192).
   - (b) Make validate() strip comments, reusing the string-aware helper at pln_chat/ontology/inventory.py:131-145, and add a validator test.
   - Route (b) also fixes an existing bug: the download's own 3-line header (patient_tab.py:190-192) already fails validation when loaded as extra_atoms, which is what the header tells the person to do. Probe output: "Symbol(s) not found: My, Not, PLN, Patient, …".

5. **The labels are not stated in the KB.**
   - No patient-diagnosis predicate exists; grep for HasCondition, Diagnosed, HasDiagnosis and PatientCondition finds nothing.
   - CoronaryHeartDisease and CongestiveHeartFailure exist only as (Inheritance X Outcome) at grim_age_lu2019_evidence.metta:11-12. They are targets of an incident 10-year risk (grim_age_lu2019_evidence.metta:28; nhanes_baseline.metta:31-33). pln_risk_prediction.metta:97-101 notes that NHANES CHD items are prevalence.
   - So "CHD -> CoronaryHeartDisease" invites predict-risk-patient for someone who already has CHD. Probe E1: the engine returns 9.8% incident CHD for a patient who typed CHD.
   - The honest label is "already diagnosed: the KB's CHD risk is for a first event and does not apply."
   - Heart failure: "LinAge2 comorbidity score only" is false. fs1 reads MCQ160B but never counts it (linage2_model.py:47-48; FS1_ITEMS at 49-55 lacks it). Yet patient_text.py:478 and 505 accept it, and the Read panel lists it without saying so.
   - The other 21 items (hypertension, stroke, osteoporosis and so on) have no KB symbol at all.

6. **Counts.** fs1 counts 22 of the 23 items it reads (linage2_model.py:47-48). patient_text's _FS1_ITEMS lists 23 (lines 505-507). ComorbidityScore already reaches the translator: patient.atoms holds (LinAgeContribution Caller_Me ComorbidityScore 0.003407 Measured), from linage2_builder.py:353-357, and three diagnoses moved it by only 0.003 years.

7. **The person already sees the diagnoses at Read.** patient_text.py:1070-1073 writes the "diagnoses: …" note and patient_tab.py:106-107 displays it. The gain is on the translator side only.

8. **The scout's probe tests a path that never carries the patient.** `infer` on the full stack is not a patient form, and patient_atoms_for (patient_context.py:82-88) would not inject the patient there at all.

9. **Effort.** Route (a) is S to M: payload key, builder field, prompt prose, a 23-item label table, a rule in pln_chat/prompts/system_prompt.txt, and tests. Route (b) adds S for the validator change and its test. New head symbols: 0 (confirmed).

Still needed:

- A test that the file is absent from _INFERENCE_STACK, like the one for LINAGE2_LAYER_FILES (:212).

The headroom is fine. As a file plus a 32-head pad, it answers rc 0 in both the LinAge2 stack and the patient stack.

2. THE BUILDER PLUMBING IS LARGER THAN LISTED.
- compute_linage2 keeps the per-input z as a local (pln_chat/core/linage2_model.py:297-300). LinAge2Result (:115-124) does not return it.
- ParsedPatient.kb_markers() (pln_chat/core/patient_text.py:279-312) never sees that result. The z has to be exposed or recomputed, and emitted only when albumin was typed (measured).
- A z-only MarkerSpec in MARKERS (pln_chat/core/patient_builder.py:97) makes Hypoalbuminemia a public marker that any caller can send, and it appears in marker_catalog.
- A z passed directly is derived=False, so the "pooled reference, not age/sex-adjusted" warning (patient_builder.py:640-657) will not fire. A provenance note is needed.

3. EXISTING TESTS, BATTERY AND DOCS THAT SAY "ALBUMIN IS UNEXPLAINED" WILL BREAK. This happens as soon as (MeasuresBiomarker SerumAlbumin Hypoalbuminemia) is added, even with no z. Probe: six-labs with the file and no witness z gives "(ReadsOut Hypoalbuminemia (witnessed False)) (DrivenBy ())", and no lever moves. These must be updated:
- tests/test_linage2.py:490, which asserts (ReadsOut None).
- scripts/linage2_battery.py:269-274 (c_decomp_top requires reads_out is None).
- The "Only FOUR" comment at linage2_core.metta:244-245.
- docs/linage2_integration.md:130-134 and :264.

4. THE LABEL AND THRESHOLD ARE A CLINICAL DECISION, NOT A DETAIL. On the model's own reference (age 50 and under), the male median is 46 g/L and the female median 44 g/L, with a scaled MAD of 2.965. - Clinical hypoalbuminemia is below 3.5 g/dL. Both tab examples (4.1 and 3.8 g/dL) are clinically normal, yet the person would see "Hypoalbuminemia … Elevated".
- The model's imputed (cohort-median) albumin for a 75-year-old man is 44 g/L, already close to the cut.

- The 58M "-1.35 age-matched" figure in the risks was not verified.
